Title: Understanding Model Calibration - A gentle introduction and visual exploration of calibration and the expected calibration error (ECE)
In this blogpost we consider a classification task with KK possible classes, with labels Y∈{1,…,K}Y\in\{1,...,K\} and a classification model p^:𝒳→ΔK\hat{p}:\mathscr{X}\rightarrow\Delta^{K}, that takes inputs in 𝒳\mathscr{X} (e.g. an image or text) and returns a probability vector as its output. The left chart below visualises the perfectly calibrated outcome (green diagonal line) for all confidences using a binned reliability diagram (Guo et al., 2017). If the model correctly classifies 7 out of 10 predictions (true), it is considered calibrated at confidence level 0.70.7. One widely used evaluation measure for confidence calibration is the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) (Naeini et al., 2015; Guo et al., 2017). ECE measures how well a model’s estimated probabilities match the observed probabilities by taking a weighted average over the absolute difference between average accuracy (acc) and average confidence (conf). Only the maximum probabilities, which determine the predicted label are used in ECE (Guo et al., 2017). For instance, if a model always predicts the majority class with that class’s average prevalence as the probability, it will have an ECE of 0. instance-level calibration errors of correct and wrong predictions (Si et al., 2022) and. The idea that more than just the maximum confidence should be calibrated, is best illustrated with a simple example (Vaicenavicius et al., 2019):. The existing concept of calibration as ”confidence calibration” (coined in (Kull et al., 2019)) makes a distinction between two additional interpretations of confidence: multi-class and class-wise calibration. A model is considered multi-class calibrated if, for any prediction vector q=(q1,…,qK)∈ΔKq=(q\_{1},...,q\_{K})\in\Delta^{K}, the class proportions among. This shift towards training models on collective annotator views, rather than relying on a single source-of-truth motivates another definition of calibration: calibrating the model against human uncertainty (Baan et al., 2022). A model is considered human-uncertainty calibrated if, for each specific sample xx, the predicted probability for each class k matches the ’actual’ probability Pv​o​t​eP\_{vote} of that class being correct. If the human labelled distribution yiy\_{i} matches this predicted vector then this sample is considered calibrated. To evaluate human uncertainty calibration (Baan et al., 2022) introduce three new measures: the Human Entropy Calibration Error (EntCE), the Human Ranking Calibration Score (RankCS) and the Human Distribution Calibration Error (DistCE).

results.content: # uncertainty-calibration 0.1.4. Utilities to calibrate model uncertainties and measure calibration. # Uncertainty Calibration Library. This repository contains library code to measure the calibration error of models, including confidence intervals computed by Bootstrap resampling, and code to recalibrate models. Our functions estimate the calibration error and ECE more accurately than prior "plugin" estimators and we provide Bootstrap confidence intervals. See Verified Uncertainty Calibration for more details. Motivating example for uncertainty calibration: Calster and Vickers 2015 train a random forest that takes in features such as tumor size and presence of teratoma, and tries to predict the probability a patient has testicular cancer. Calibration is a popular way to measure the quality of a model's uncertainties, and recalibration is a way to take an existing model and correct its uncertainties to make them better. This library focuses on calibration for classification tasks. Measuring the calibration error of a model is as simple as:. Our library makes it very easy to measure confidence intervals on the calibration error as well, using bootstrap resamples. ## Advanced: ECE, Debiasing, and Top-Label Calibration Error. By default, our library measure per-class, root-mean-squared calibration error, and uses the techniques in Verified Uncertainty Calibration to accurately estimate the calibration error. However, we also support measuring the ECE (Guo et al) and using older, less accurate, ways of estimating the calibration error. get_top_calibration_error(model_probs, labels, p = 1). Multiclass calibration vs ECE / Top-label: When measuring the calibration error of a multiclass model, we can measure the calibration error of all classes (per-class calibration error), or of the top prediction. ## Verified Uncertainty Calibration paper. This repository also contains code for the NeurIPS 2019 (Spotlight) paper Verified Uncertainty Calibration. * The calibration error of methods like Platt scaling and temperature scaling are typically underestimated, and cannot be easily measured. * We propose an efficient recalibration method where the calibration error can be measured. * Experiments showing the debiased estimator can estimate calibration error with fewer samples than standard estimator (Section 5) Running each experiment saves plots in the corresponding folder in saved\_files. uncertainty-calibration-0..gz (15.9 kB view details). Details for the file `uncertainty-calibration-0..gz`. * Download URL: uncertainty-calibration-0..gz. Hashes for uncertainty-calibration-0..gz.
